title: biomolecules-and-cell-biology Mindmap
topicTitle: biomolecules and cell biology — interactive concept map
notes: Biomolecules are the chemical basis of life. Carbohydrates supply and store energy and form structural fibres; proteins (from 20 amino acids) act as enzymes,…
Biomolecules are organic molecules essential to life: carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, plus minerals, enzymes and water.
Carbohydrates (CH2O)n: monosaccharides (glucose, fructose, ribose), disaccharides (sucrose=glucose+fructose, lactose, maltose), polysaccharides (starch,…

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Functions: C=energy+structure, P=enzymes/transport/structure, L=storage+membrane, N=heredity+protein…
A hydrolysis breaks a bond + water; a condensation joins molecules - water.
Enzymes are specific, reversible regulators, not consumed in the reaction.
DNA is the gene; RNA is the messenger/scaffold in protein synthesis.
Essential amino acids (8 in adults, 9 in children) must come from food.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: General carbohydrate ratio: C : H : O = 1 : 2 : 1, i.e. (CH2O)n
Endergonic polymerisation (condensation): monomer + monomer → dimer + H2O
Peptide unit: -C(=O)-NH-
DNA base pairing: A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds)

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: All cells share the same basic biochemical machinery of DNA→RNA→protein (central dogma).
The 20 naturally occurring L-amino acids differ only in their R-group (side chain).
Phospholipid bilayers form spontaneously because the head is hydrophilic and the tail is hydrophobic.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: High frequency: monomer/polymer matching tables, enzyme action and factors affecting enzymes.
Diagram-based marks: label a phospholipid bilayer and a DNA nucleotide.
Application: explain a disease caused by a biomolecule deficiency.
Remember C-H-O-N: C=energy, P=work, L=lipid, N=genetic.
A-T two H-bonds (think "A" has 2 strokes), G-C three.

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: Cellulose is a structural polymer in plant cell walls, not an energy reserve; glycogen (animal) and starch…
Starch is unbranched amylose + branched amylopectin; both yield maltose on hydrolysis.
Ribose and deoxyribose differ only by one oxygen atom on C-2; hence RNA vs DNA sugars.

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Cell = smallest structural + functional unit of life.
Prokaryote: no nucleus, 70S ribosomes, circular DNA, cell wall usually peptidoglycan.
Eukaryote: membrane-bound nucleus, 80S ribosomes, linear chromosomes, organelles.
Three postulates of cell theory (Schleiden, Schwann, Virchow).
Cell wall: plants (cellulose), fungi (chitin), bacteria (peptidoglycan); absent in animals.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: General size: prokaryote ~ 1-10 µm; eukaryote ~ 10-100 µm
Magnification = image size ÷ real size

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: All known living organisms are cellular.
A prokaryote is the simplest true cell; a eukaryote is the most complex.
The plasma membrane is selectively permeable and controls the entry of materials.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Prokaryote/eukaryote comparison table is a very common short-answer.
State cell theory fully (3 postulates + names).
Describe the structure of a typical bacterium with a labelled diagram.
PRO = small, NO nucleus; EU = nucleus + organelles.
Ribosome 7-0 (seventy) = prokaryote; 8-0 = eukaryote.

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: A virus is not a cell and is not prokaryotic or eukaryotic; it is an acellular, obligate intracellular…
Prokaryotes lack a nuclear membrane but still carry DNA (usually a single circular chromosome).
Mycoplasma has no cell wall; it is the smallest known living cell (0.1-0.3 µm), not the smallest living…

RER = rough = ribosomes = protein; SER = smooth = no ribosomes = lipid.
Mitochondria + chloroplast: own DNA, 70S ribosomes, double membrane, binary fission (endosymbiosis).
Protein-secretion pathway: ribosome → RER → Golgi → vesicle → membrane.
Plant cell: wall + chloroplast + large central vacuole; animal cell: centrioles + lysosomes + small vacuoles.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Fluid-mosaic: phospholipid bilayer + integral/peripheral protein + cholesterol + glycocalyx
Protein secretion: ribosome → RER → Golgi → vesicle → exocytosis
Mitochondrial respiration: glycolysis → Krebs → ETS → ~34 ATP
9+9 axoneme (cilia/flagella); 9+0 centriole

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: The plasma membrane is the selectively permeable boundary of every cell.
Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration; chloroplasts of photosynthesis.
The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids.

points: Each organelle has a distinct, frequently-examined function (mitochondrion→ATP, chloroplast→photosynthesis).
RER makes protein; SER makes lipid; Golgi packages; lysosome digests.
Plasma membrane is selectively permeable fluid mosaic.
Nucleus + nucleolus + chromatin = genetic control; chromatin condenses into chromosomes.

Cilia and flagella use a 9+9 microtubule arrangement for locomotion.

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: The cell wall is fully permeable; the plasma membrane is selectively permeable.
RER is rough because of ribosomes; it makes PROTEINS. SER makes LIPIDS and detoxifies — it has no ribosomes.
The Golgi packages proteins and lipids; it does not synthesise them.

branches.topic: Cell Division — Cycle, Mitosis and Meiosis

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Cell cycle: G1, S, G2 (interphase) + M; checkpoints prevent errors.
PMAT = Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase of mitosis.
Meiosis: two divisions; crossing over (Prophase I) + independent assortment (Metaphase I) create variation.
Anaphase I separates homologs; Anaphase (mitosis) + Anaphase II separate sister chromatids.
Cytokinesis: animal (cleavage furrow) vs plant (cell plate).

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Mitosis: 2n → 2 daughter cells of 2n
Meiosis: 2n → 4 gametes of n
Crossing over (Prophase I) + independent assortment (Metaphase I) → variation
Chromosome count: after S each chromosome = 2 chromatids

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Mitosis maintains a species' diploid chromosome number.
Meiosis halves the genome and shuffles alleles, creating variation.
The cell cycle is controlled by checkpoints that stop M phase if DNA is damaged.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Draw and label all four mitotic phases.
Draw a full meiosis diagram (mark crossing over + independent assortment).
Tabulate mitosis vs meiosis (6 points).
PMAT = Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase.
MITO = 2 identical (2n); MEI = 4 different (n).

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: Mitosis maintains the chromosome number (2n → 2n); meiosis halves it (2n → n).
Crossing over and independent assortment occur in MEIOSIS only, not mitosis.
